title: Sides and Corners
short: Compare shapes by counting their sides and corners.

blocks.html: You know flat shapes and you can count. Counting sides and corners helps you name and compare shapes.

blocks.name: k-pic
blocks.cap: The gold dots mark the corners.

blocks.html: A side is a straight edge. A corner is where two sides meet. A shape with straight sides has the same number of sides and corners.
Each side ends at a corner, and the next side starts there. Going around the shape, you meet one corner after each side, so the numbers match.

blocks.title: A hexagon
blocks.q: How many sides and corners does a hexagon have?
steps: Put a finger on one side and go around: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6.

blocks.name: geoboard
blocks.cap: Drag a corner. The shape changes, but it still has 3 sides and 3 corners.

blocks.html: For grown-ups: Build shapes with straws or craft sticks. Count the sides and corners together.

sources.name: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics, Kindergarten, K.G.B.4: analyze and compare shapes using their parts, such as the number of sides and corners
